story.what_it_is: Old fixed text fields, like app name and vendor, that still differ a little by system and engine.
story.for_you: You never see them. They are mostly frozen for old websites. A few still differ between systems, which lets a site cross check that you are who your browser says you are.
story.for_makers: These strings exist so old sites do not break. Modern sites use them in consistency checks. When privacy tools or bots change one value but forget another, the mismatch stands out.

use_cases.example: A bot defence service checks that the vendor, platform and user agent agree and challenges those that do not.
An ad fraud vendor verifies that browser identity strings are consistent before counting a view.
An old script reads appName and appVersion to guess the browser, which still works for basic cases.
A bank risk engine adds suspicion when two strings disagree.
A fingerprinting library mixes the strings into a device ID.
A browser games platform checks these strings to pick the right controls layout for the engine.
